title: Enable suppression of `RequiresMountsFor` for volumes in quadlets
body:
### Feature request description

Quadlets automatically generate `RequiresMountsFor` for all specified volumes in service unit file. This is unfortunate for containers mounting automount shares. If the share is unmounted, the container gets automatically stopped by systemd (via propagation). I have a backup share mounted in the container and the container is stopped every some hours 

### Suggest potential solution

I want to be able to mark volumes to not generate `RequiresMountsFor=...`. This could either be done via a mount switch (`:opt`) or with a quadlet line suppressing some or all `RequiresMountsFor=...` generation (e.g. via (`OptionalVolume=`).

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Alternatives are to stay either directly on .service files (not taking advantage of organized Quadlets) or mounting a parent folder of the automount share. Both options are not suitable. Switching to a fixed mount does also not work in my case.

### Additional context

_No response_

comments.body:
I feel like an option the under [Quadlet] section might be best, we already have `DefaultDependencies` there.
Or maybe we could also make default `DefaultDependencies=no` also count for the RequiresMountsFor line since these are another form of default deps?

cc @ygalblum

@Luap99 your suggestions makes sense. However, as always with these changes, the fear is with breaking current usage. If you think it's fine to add this dependency into the skipped ones, I'm fine with it as well.

Yeah I am not sure it makes sense to include that under the DefaultDependencies, backwards compat is a concern, also people might like to treat both separately the network dep and the RequiresMountsFor so having two keys might be more logical and less risky but not sure what a good name would be.
`SetRequiresMountsFor=yes/no` where it default to yes (true) to keep the current behavior. It would then be global for all mounts.
Users would only want `RequiresMountsFor=` for a specific mount could still simply do `SetRequiresMountsFor=no` and then list `RequiresMountsFor=` manually under [Unit] only for the they want it and not all.

If a separate option is introduced, maybe `SetMountsDependency=[Requires|Wants|None]` would be suitable (with default=Requires) instead of yes/no. This would keep compatibility and could enable WantsMountsFor behaviour, which is good for normal mounts but will not stop the container if unmounted.
